html:
Sulaiman-Too is a rocky mountain rising above the city of Osh in the Fergana valley of Kyrgyzstan, a holy place since long before Islam and the country's first World Heritage Site.

Its slopes carry ancient rock carvings and caves linked to cults of fertility and healing. In Muslim times it was named after Solomon, a prophet in Islam, and it drew pilgrims who believed it marked his grave. The young Babur, later founder of the Mughal Empire, built a small prayer house on top in the 1490s, rebuilt in modern times.

Osh, at its foot, is one of the oldest cities in Central Asia, a market town on the routes through the Fergana valley. In 2010 it was the centre of the bloody clashes between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks.
sum: Sulaiman-Too is a rocky mountain rising above the city of Osh in the Fergana valley of Kyrgyzstan, a holy place since long before Islam and the country's first World Heritage Site.
